title: Robust schema and streaming handoff contracts for tool/function calls
creator: Maya Chen
description: PRD fragment: Define acceptance criteria, error modes, and rollout steps for the new structured-output + tool-calling runtime contracts. This ticket captures the product-level requirements for streaming JSON/object envelopes, schema version negotiation, partial-object emission semantics, and the expected behavior when invoking external tools or internal function call endpoints. The aim is to make streaming structured responses reliable for client parsing, resilient under partial failures and backpressure, and observable in Console. This is intentionally scoped to interface and acceptance criteria (not implementation details).
scope_changes: Initial scope included only schema shape and success path. Added streaming partial-emission behavior and explicit error envelope rules after design review (2025-01-28). Also expanded acceptance criteria to include rollback and canary metrics for runtime rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Schema negotiation: Producer advertises schema_version in the initial metadata frame; consumer must accept or request fallback within 50ms. Successful negotiation logged to tracing with schema_version and negotiated_version.

Streaming envelopes: Every stream must emit a top-level 'envelope' object when streaming structured output. Envelope MUST include: kind (stream|final|error), schema_version, id (UUID), and optionally 'partial' boolean when content is incremental.

Partial object semantics: For partial=true emissions, objects must be JSON-mergeable in order. Clients should be able to reconstruct the final object by applying successive partials. Runtime to guarantee monotonic key addition or clearly documented overwrite semantics in acceptance tests.

Tool call initiation: When model initiates a tool/function call, stream MUST include a 'tool_call' envelope with tool_name, tool_args (validated against registered schema), call_id, and expected idempotency_hint. A separate 'tool_response' envelope with matching call_id is required when the tool returns.

Idempotency and retries: Tool gateway must accept idempotency_hint and must make best-effort to deduplicate retries. Acceptance tests will verify that repeated identical call requests with same idempotency_hint produce the same recorded outcome or a documented reconciliation error.

Error envelopes and fallback: On transient tool failure, emit an 'error' envelope with error_type: transient|permanent|timeout, human_message, machine_code, and optional 'retry_after_ms'. If error_type is transient, the runtime should attempt configured fallback (alternate tool or model variant) and emit 'fallback_attempt' envelopes.

Backpressure and client read-slow handling: If consumer read window is saturated, runtime emits 'paused' and 'resumed' envelopes. Stream must not deadlock; a paused stream that remains unread for >30s triggers a 'server_aborted' envelope and a post-mortem entry.

Streaming parseability: Clients using incremental JSON parsers (ndjson or chunked JSON with envelope boundaries) must be able to verify each envelope independently. Acceptance test will run sample parsers in JS and Go against produced streams to confirm correctness.

Schema evolution: Producers may emit 'deprecated_fields' warnings in metadata for 90 days. Acceptance tests will assert backward compat behavior by running consumer suites against previous schema versions.

Observability and SLOs: Console must expose a 'schema_error_rate' metric (errors per 10k envelopes), 'tool_call_failure_rate', and median time-to-first-envelope. Rollout gate: schema_error_rate < 0.1% and tool_call_failure_rate < 1% for canary before broad rollout.

E2E tests: A deterministic golden test that streams a 12-envelope conversation with interleaved tool calls, partial object patches, a transient tool failure with fallback, and final consolidated object is required. Golden must be versioned and checked into tests/structured-output/goldens.

Documentation & SDKs: Developer docs updated with code samples for streaming envelopes and SDK helpers (JS/Go/Python) that rehydrate partial objects. Docs must include a migration guide for schema_version changes.
decisions: Adopt explicit envelope boundary model (single envelope per line) instead of concatenated JSON objects without markers to simplify incremental parsing.
Use a limited set of standardized machine_code strings for error envelopes (TOOL_TIMEOUT, TOOL_500, SCHEMA_MISMATCH, BACKPRESSURE).
Fallback policy: prefer alternate tool within same tenant region; fall back to model-variant only if alternate tool unavailable.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (Canary): Enable structured streaming for 5% of hosts in runtime-1.21 for internal customers; monitor schema_error_rate and tool_call_failure_rate for 72 hours.
Stage 2 (Beta): Expand to 25% with opt-in for external early-access customers; collect SDK parsing telemetry and address issues.
Stage 3 (GA): Full rollout after two successful betas and meeting SLO gates; publish migration guide and enable default parsing helpers in SDKs.
qa_checks: Run JS and Go incremental parser suites against golden streams; diff output objects against expected final object.
Simulate tool gateway transient failures and verify fallback envelopes and idempotency behavior.
Inject slow consumer scenarios and assert 'paused'/'resumed' behavior and eventual server_aborted emission on timeout.
Verify telemetry emitted for each envelope: envelope_kind, schema_version, call_id (if present), and latency_ms to consumer.
